dsfit: Fit and Compare Detection Functions for Line-Transect Survey Data

Source: R/dsfit-package.R
dsfit-package.Rd

Fits a set of candidate detection functions to line-transect distance data and compares them on the quantities that matter for abundance, not on AIC alone. Models are fitted through 'mrds' so that every candidate comes off the same likelihood machinery and the gamma key function is available alongside half-normal, hazard-rate and uniform. Enforces the conditions under which a comparison is meaningful: truncation must be held constant within a model set, and binned and exact distances cannot be ranked together. Reports effective strip half-width and its coefficient of variation next to each fit, since two models within two AIC of one another can imply materially different abundance. Takes the flatfile produced by 'distsamp' or any equivalent table.

Main functions

model_set()

Builds the grid of candidate detection functions.

diagnose_sweep()

Checks data and a model set for common problems before anything is fitted.

prepare_distance_data()

Validates distances and applies the truncation. Called by sweep_models(); also usable on its own.

sweep_models()

Fits every candidate with mrds::ddf() and builds a selection table.

selection_table()

Returns the ranked table from a sweep.

detection_structure()

Reports what a table of detections can support, such as exact or binned distances and double-observer data.

availability(), g0()

Build a g(0) correction from external data, for use at the abundance step.

Where the package sits

dsfit is the middle of three layers. distsamp turns NARWC-format survey data into effort segments and detection distances. dsfit fits and compares detection functions. A separate analysis repository holds the per-run choices: years, truncation, covariates. Logic that can be tested lives in the package; project-specific choices do not.

Why models are fitted through mrds

Distance::ds() is a good tool for fitting one model interactively, and dsfit does not replace it. ds() offers only the hn, hr and unif keys. The gamma key, which suits a platform that cannot see directly beneath itself, is available only in mrds. Fitting every candidate through mrds::ddf() also means every AIC in a selection table comes from the same likelihood code, with the same handling of truncation and monotonicity.

g(0) is not estimated

g(0) is the probability of detecting an animal on the track-line. Every fit assumes g(0) = 1. A wrong g(0) scales every candidate by the same factor, so the model ranking is unchanged while density is biased. g(0) cannot be estimated from sighting distances alone. Availability needs dive data, and perception needs a double-observer design that some NARWC programmes recorded and many did not; detection_structure() reports which a given extract has. Apply the correction at the abundance step, from external sources, and propagate its standard error. availability() and g0() build that correction.
